papers.title: "Take Me Home, Wi-Fi Drone": A Drone-based Wireless System for Wilderness Search and Rescue
papers.abstract: Wilderness Search and Rescue (WiSAR) represents a longstanding and critical societal challenge, demanding innovative and automatic technological solutions. In this paper, we introduce Wi2SAR, a novel autonomous drone-based wireless system for long-range, through-occlusion WiSAR operations, without relying on existing infrastructure. Our basic insight is to leverage the automatic reconnection behavior of modern Wi-Fi devices to known networks. By mimicking these networks via on-drone Wi-Fi, Wi2SAR uniquely facilitates the discovery and localization of victims through their accompanying mobile devices. Translating this simple idea into a practical system poses substantial technical challenges. Wi2SAR overcomes these challenges via three distinct innovations: (1) a rapid and energy-efficient device discovery mechanism to discover and identify the target victim, (2) a novel RSS-only, long-range direction finding approach using a 3D-printed Luneburg Lens, amplifying the directional signal strength differences and significantly extending the operational range, and (3) an adaptive drone navigation scheme that guides the drone toward the target efficiently. We implement an end-to-end prototype and evaluate Wi2SAR across various mobile devices and real-world wilderness scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate Wi2SAR's high performance, efficiency, and practicality, highlighting its potential to advance autonomous WiSAR solutions. Wi2SAR is open-sourced at https://aiot-lab.github.io/Wi2SAR to facilitate further research and real-world deployment.
papers.title_text: "Take Me Home, Wi-Fi Drone": A Drone-based Wireless System for Wilderness Search and Rescue

papers.title: A First Look at Multimodal Mobile Application Performance on XR and AI Smart Glasses
papers.abstract: Smart glasses are the next mobile platform. Unlike phones, glasses operate as sensing-first devices that route data through a multi-hop wireless pipeline: a constrained glass to companion puck or a phone short-range edge link and cloud AI backends. This architecture exposes an entirely new class of wireless and mobile system problems that the community has not yet confronted. We present the first in-depth measurement study across several glasses and core XR and AI applications. Our findings open up rich problems for the community in rethinking glass-phone-cloud architecture and reimagining how smartphones can serve as efficient edge servers for the next generation of wearable computing.

papers.title: ActiveSight: Enabling Continuous Wearable Perception through Algorithm-Hardware Co-Designed Multimodal Semantic Gating
papers.abstract: Continuous wearable AI perception must capture transient, meaningful events throughout the day, yet always-on visual processing rapidly exhausts batteries of compact wearables. We present ActiveSight, an algorithm-hardware co-designed multimodal gating system that exploits the complementarity between audio and vision: audio is energy-efficient but perceptually limited, while vision is accurate but too power-hungry to run continuously. ActiveSight uses a low-power audio front-end as an always-on trigger and activates a unified CLIP-based detector only when visual semantic filtering is needed. The detector performs keyword-guided semantic filtering with reconfigurable text anchors, transmitting only relevant frames without on-device retraining. To enable on-wearable execution, we design a custom FPGA accelerator featuring the PatchDW dataflow, which mitigates the memory bottleneck of depthwise convolutions and achieves 44.3 GOPS/W in PL-side active power. Evaluation on Ego4D shows that ActiveSight achieves 87.7% event hit rate at 453 mW average power, reduces average power by 3× compared with continuous visual streaming, and reaches 88.5% hit rate in live smart-glasses deployment.
papers.title_text: ActiveSight: Enabling Continuous Wearable Perception through Algorithm-Hardware Co-Designed Multimodal Semantic Gating

papers.title: Adaptive Segmented Decentralized Federated Learning on Tiny Devices
papers.abstract: We present tinyGist, an efficient decentralized federated learning framework designed for tiny microcontrollers. Instead of treating all model parameters equally, each device exchanges a portion of them, effectively sharing a “gist” of the information. Our major contributions are: (1) segment model parameters based on their importance, while identifying the most impactful updates, (2) share the gist probabilistically, maintaining model diversity while ensuring fast knowledge propagation across peers, (3) update models based on the information merit received from other neighbors, and (4) adaptive learning. We implement tinyGist across various simulation experiments, large-scale realistic emulation with hundreds of devices, and real deployment on homogeneous and heterogeneous physical microcontroller clusters. Evaluated on eight machine learning models and 15 tasks, tinyGist outperforms existing baselines in convergence speed by 1.35–3.3× and accuracy by up to 17%, while reducing communication overhead by ≈3× compared to the full-model baselines. We further validate our lightweight importance proxy against gradient-, Fisher-, and Hessian-based measures, and characterize how tinyGist interacts with differential privacy and secure aggregation.
papers.title_text: Adaptive Segmented Decentralized Federated Learning on Tiny Devices

papers.title: AppFlow: Memory Scheduling for Cold Launch of Large Apps on Mobile and Vehicle Systems
papers.abstract: GB-scale large apps like on-device LLMs and rich media editors are becoming the next-generation trend, but their heavy memory and I/O demands, especially during multitasking, cause devices to reclaim or kill processes, turning warm apps into cold launches. The challenge lies not in storing them, but in fast, accurate launching. For users, 1s is the usability cliff, yet our measurements show 86.6% of GB-scale cold launches exceed it. Also, Android Vitals flags only ≥5s as slow, exposing a large satisfaction gap. Existing optimizations are designed in isolation and conflict. For example, preloading reduces I/O stalls but consumes scarce memory and is undone by reclamation, while reclamation and killing free memory but sacrifice background survivability, leading to repeated cold relaunches. Our key insight is that, although multitasking makes runtime behavior complex, each app's file access pattern remains predictable. The challenge lies in exploiting this predictability, i.e., preloading without exhausting memory, reclaiming without undoing gains, and killing selectively to preserve background survivability. We introduce AppFlow, a prediction-based system-wide scheduler that integrates a Selective File Preloader, an Adaptive Memory Reclaimer, and a Context-Aware Process Killer. Implemented across the Android framework and Linux kernel without app changes, AppFlow cuts GB-scale cold-launch latency by 66.5% (e.g., 2s→690ms) and sustains 95% of launches within 1s over a 100-day test, significantly improving responsiveness and multitasking experience.
papers.title_text: AppFlow: Memory Scheduling for Cold Launch of Large Apps on Mobile and Vehicle Systems

papers.title: ATM-SLAM: Adaptive Temporal Memory Visual SLAM in Severe Rainy Conditions
papers.abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (vSLAM) plays a crucial role in autonomous vehicles and robotics by enabling real-time localization and mapping in unknown environments. However, as current vSLAM systems are primarily designed for ideal weather conditions they often experience significant accuracy degradation and sudden operational breakdowns in severe rainy conditions (> 10 mm/h), posing serious safety hazards. To fill the gap, we propose ATM-SLAM, a novel learning-based vSLAM framework that overcomes the intense visual interference under severe rainy conditions and enhances system robustness. ATM-SLAM incorporates two key modules: (i) an Adaptive Feature Encoder (AFE), which adaptively prioritizes rain-robust features across consecutive frames, (ii) a Temporal Memory Integration (TMI) module, which integrates memorized correlation information to recover and stabilize localization under distorted frames. We extensively evaluate ATM-SLAM on a consumer vehicle, a robotic platform, and widely used public datasets across diverse scenarios. The evaluation results demonstrate that ATM-SLAM can achieve accurate and reliable localization and mapping in heavy rain. Moreover, to facilitate future research on vSLAM under severe rainy conditions, we collected the Severe Rainy SLAM Dataset (SR-SLAM), a large-scale real-world dataset, and plan to release it as a dedicated benchmark for evaluating vSLAM robustness.
papers.title_text: ATM-SLAM: Adaptive Temporal Memory Visual SLAM in Severe Rainy Conditions

papers.title: Attacking mmWave Imaging Using Metasurfaces Based on Intensity and Time-of-Flight Manipulation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an efficient attack on millimeter-wave (mmWave) security screening systems by designing a novel reflective metasurface, termed MagicPatch, which is applied to prohibited items hidden under clothing and alters imaging results to resemble those of the human body, significantly reducing detection rates. In wideband mmWave imaging systems, MagicPatch is optimized in two key aspects: (1) tuning group delay parameters to manipulate the Time-of-Flight (i.e., perceived object distance); and (2) adjusting reflectivity to control the intensity of the reflected signals (i.e., material properties). To enable automated MagicPatch design, we propose a joint optimization framework that determines the optimal structural configurations of the MagicPatch for targeted attack scenarios, while supporting a low-cost fabrication process. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on two commercial mmWave security scanners with volunteers of diverse body types. The results demonstrate that the MagicPatch effectively conceals eight types of prohibited items with thicknesses ranging from 1 to 5 cm, achieving an alarm suppression rate of 85.7% to 97.0%, significantly higher than baseline methods at 9.4% to 36.7%.
papers.title_text: Attacking mmWave Imaging Using Metasurfaces Based on Intensity and Time-of-Flight Manipulation

papers.title: Breaking Coordinate Overfitting: Geometry-Aware WiFi Sensing for Cross-Layout 3D Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: WiFi-based 3D human pose estimation offers a low-cost and privacy-preserving alternative to vision-based systems for smart interaction. However, existing approaches rely on visual 3D poses as supervision and directly regress CSI to a camera-based coordinate system. We find that this practice leads to coordinate overfitting: models memorize deployment-specific WiFi transceiver layouts rather than only learning activity-relevant representations, resulting in severe generalization failures. To address this challenge, we present PerceptAlign, the first geometry-conditioned framework for WiFi-based cross-layout pose estimation. PerceptAlign introduces a lightweight coordinate unification procedure that aligns WiFi and vision measurements in a shared 3D space using only two checkerboards and a few photos. Within this unified space, it encodes calibrated transceiver positions into high-dimensional embeddings and fuses them with CSI features, making the model explicitly aware of device geometry as a conditional variable. This design forces the network to disentangle human motion from deployment layouts, enabling robust and, for the first time, layout-invariant WiFi pose estimation. To support systematic evaluation, we construct the largest cross-domain 3D WiFi pose estimation dataset. Experiments show that PerceptAlign reduces cross-domain error by more than 60% compared to state-of-the-art baselines. These results establish geometry-conditioned learning as a viable path toward practical WiFi sensing.
papers.title_text: Breaking Coordinate Overfitting: Geometry-Aware WiFi Sensing for Cross-Layout 3D Pose Estimation

papers.title: Cellulars Go Underground: Practical Obstacles and Effective Mitigation
papers.abstract: Underground cellulars are arguably the most sophisticated public network utilities in modern metropolises due to constrained environments and mobility-driven use cases. To date, their QoS has been largely unsatisfactory to users, especially on subway trains where video apps encounter frequent and lasting video stream stalls (VSSes). With the goal of deeply understanding and practically boosting underground cellular QoS, we conduct the first large-scale study of underground cellular networks, spanning 207 subway lines, 82K BSes, and 1.8M Android phones. Our study reveals the unique multi-stage signal attenuation pattern and the defective infrastructure deployment in today's subway cellular environments, which collectively contribute as the major causes of VSSes. To address this, we enable user devices to actively adapt to the environmental changes, and develop a comprehensive radio/link state collection module to effectively inform video apps. Our optimizations on device-side Android cellular management have reduced 39% VSSes in subway networks; our collaborative optimizations with popular video apps have further reduced 23% VSSes.
papers.title_text: Cellulars Go Underground: Practical Obstacles and Effective Mitigation

papers.title: CFMoE: Cache-Friendly Mixture of Experts Model Serving System on Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) on edge devices has garnered significant attention due to their inherent privacy and security benefits. However, the enormous parameter scale of modern LLMs poses fundamental challenges for resource-constrained edge devices. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models emerge as a promising solution by dynamically activating only a subset of experts during inference, and thus enhance computational efficiency. Nevertheless, the runtime uncertainty in expert activation still leads to high memory demands during inference. To address this, prior works concentrate on either compressing or offloading experts, all striving around the tradeoffs among the model precision, memory consumption, and serving throughput, and thus form an “impossible triangle”.
papers.title_text: CFMoE: Cache-Friendly Mixture of Experts Model Serving System on Edge Devices

papers.title: City-Scale Radiance-Field Reconstruction via Mixture of Radio Experts
papers.abstract: Accurately modeling the radiance field of 5G signals in urban environments is essential for reliable network operation and scalable planning of next-generation wireless systems. Recent advances in neural radiance fields (NeRF2) have shown great success in capturing the spatially continuous behavior of radio propagation. However, existing NeRF2 frameworks remain limited to small-scale scenes, suffering from severe accuracy degradation and prohibitive computational costs when extended to city-scale deployments. In this work, we present Mixture of Radio Experts (MoRE), a mixture-of-experts architecture designed for city-scale 5G radiance field reconstruction. MoRE integrates two complementary components: (i) a Mixture of Cell Experts, where each expert captures localized attenuation effects within distinct geographic regions; and (ii) a Mixture of Radiance Experts, which leverages shared and dynamically routed experts to model diverse propagation phenomena. To evaluate MoRE, we conducted a large-scale measurement campaign comprising 7,073,565 timestamped and geotagged RF samples from 13,602 base stations across 1,900 km2 in a tier-one city. Experimental results show that MoRE delivers up to a 16 dB improvement over standard NeRF2 by scaling from 0.69 million to 300 million parameters, while activating only 0.28% of the parameters (about 0.85 million) per inference.
papers.title_text: City-Scale Radiance-Field Reconstruction via Mixture of Radio Experts

papers.title: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained edge platforms is often dominated by expert-weight movement rather than computation. Although each token activates only a small subset of experts, routing is input-dependent, so all experts must remain accessible and memory movement dominates latency. Existing approaches such as uniform pruning and expert dropping overlook two properties of MoE execution: expert combinations are highly skewed in frequency, and experts contribute asymmetrically within each combination. We present CRISP, a combination-aware framework that co-designs pruning and runtime scheduling for efficient MoE serving on memory-constrained edge platforms. CRISP reorders neurons by importance so one stored expert can support multiple execution widths, assigns differentiated execution to hot, warm, and cold combinations based on frequency and expert role, and exploits heterogeneous widths to overlap expert loading with computation. Across Mixtral-8x7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B, CRISP improves throughput by up to 2.1× at the same memory budget while limiting accuracy loss to 3.6% relative to full-width inference. Our results highlight that efficient edge MoE serving requires jointly optimizing which expert capacity is preserved and how expert execution is scheduled.
papers.title_text: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers

papers.title: Cross-Band RF Radiance Field Modeling via 3D Gaussian Splatting and Propagation Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: As multi-protocol radio-frequency (RF) environments (e.g., RFID, Wi-Fi, and 5G) become increasingly prevalent, practical RF modeling is expected to overcome single-band limitations and achieve zero-shot generalization across a broad spectrum. This requires a unified representation of frequency-dependent electromagnetic (EM) propagation rather than modeling each band separately. In this paper, we present XBandGS, a unified cross-band RF radiance field modeling framework built on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Unlike prior 3DGS-based RF modeling methods restricted to single-frequency fitting, XBandGS introduces an EM propagation Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) that disentangles and learns the frequency-specific behaviors of different physics-guided propagation modes within a given 3D environment. In addition, our approach enables the effective use of non-co-located datasets measured at various locations for different frequency bands. Trained on sparse frequencies, XBandGS can predict RF radiance fields for arbitrary unseen frequencies across a broad spectrum. We evaluate the cross-band RF Power Angular Spectrum (PAS) reconstruction capability of XBandGS across diverse 3D environments, including 7 simulated indoor scenes spanning 1–94 GHz and 6 real-world scenes (4 indoor and 2 outdoor) spanning 0.7–5.8 GHz. Results show that XBandGS achieves high-fidelity PAS reconstruction in unseen frequency bands, with an average SSIM of 0.822 on simulated traces and 0.650 on real-world datasets.
papers.title_text: Cross-Band RF Radiance Field Modeling via 3D Gaussian Splatting and Propagation Mixture-of-Experts

papers.title: D-Fault: Uncovering Disaggregation Faults in 5G RAN
papers.abstract: The disaggregation of the 5G Radio Access Network (RAN) decomposes traditional base stations into distributed components such as the centralized unit (CU) and distributed unit (DU). While this architecture improves flexibility and vendor interoperability, it also turns many control procedures into distributed workflows executed by independent state machines. We show that such executions can lead to Disaggregation Faults (DF), where specification-compliant procedure interactions drive different RAN components into inconsistent control-plane states. We present D-Fault, a testing framework that systematically uncovers DF bugs by generating adversarial interleavings of control procedures and initiating them with targeted timing. A model-guided exploration reduces the intractable search space, while verification based on externally observable behavior detects inconsistencies without access to internal states. We implement D-Fault and evaluate it on SDR-based testbeds, uncovering 17 unique DF bugs that lead to serious effects such as resource corruption and denial of service.
papers.title_text: D-Fault: Uncovering Disaggregation Faults in 5G RAN

papers.title: DeltaAR: Redundancy-Aware Object Detection for Mobile Augmented Reality
papers.abstract: Real-time object detection is essential for mobile augmented reality (AR) applications; however, modern detectors based on Vision Transformers (ViTs) incur significant computational overhead. Although edge offloading can alleviate the limited compute resources on mobile devices, the inference latency of ViT-based detection on edge servers remains a major bottleneck, causing detection results to arrive after the camera viewpoint has changed and degrading AR experiences. To address this problem, we propose DeltaAR, an edge-assisted AR object detection system that leverages AR geometry (depth maps and 6-DoF camera poses) to reduce the cost of ViT-based detection. Different from existing AR systems, DeltaAR uses sensory data available on modern AR devices to accurately identify newly exposed regions between consecutive frames. Based on this information, we design a region-aware ViT that reduces computation by processing tokens required for detecting objects in newly exposed regions and skipping redundant tokens from old regions. To preserve detection accuracy, we further introduce a lightweight token selector that retains a small set of old-region tokens needed for cross-boundary objects and contextual information. Experiments show that DeltaAR significantly reduces edge inference cost and latency while maintaining high detection accuracy for real-time AR applications.
papers.title_text: DeltaAR: Redundancy-Aware Object Detection for Mobile Augmented Reality

papers.title: DeRa: Deep-Range Low-Power Wide Area IoT via Ultra-sensitive Signal Detection
papers.abstract: LoRa extends communication range by operating well below the noise floor, yet this capability hinges on reliable packet detection—an overlooked bottleneck. Carrier frequency offset (CFO) introduces deterministic inter-chirp phase shifts that prevent coherent preamble accumulation; because all existing detectors fall back on non-coherent, magnitude-only addition, they forfeit substantial signal power. We present DeRa, a phase-coherent LoRa detection and decoding framework built on three contributions: (1) a phase-coherent detection method that exploits the relationship between CFO and inter-chirp phase evolution to detect weak packets; (2) analytical compensation of compound CFO-induced scaling distortions—timing drift, frequency migration, and energy leakage—so that coherent accumulation remains effective even under 40 kHz CFO, eliminating the need for expensive oscillator hardware; and (3) a CRC-guided, phase-compensated iterative decoder that coherently recombines split symbol energy and closes the detection-to-decoding feedback loop. On COTS LoRa devices across SF 7–12, DeRa lowers the detection threshold by 4.3–4.8 dB and the decoding threshold by 3.3–3.9 dB over state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining O(N log N) per-symbol complexity and consistent gains in real-world field experiments.
papers.title_text: DeRa: Deep-Range Low-Power Wide Area IoT via Ultra-sensitive Signal Detection

papers.title: Designing, Deployment and Field Testing of C2Stack for Networked Intelligent Software-Defined UAVs
papers.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are emerging as critical enablers of next-generation wireless networking and autonomous systems. Despite their potential, deploying and testing networked UAV systems in real-world environments remains challenging, largely due to the absence of well-developed, end-to-end, ready-to-use protocol stacks. To fill this gap, we present C2Stack, a configurable protocol stack and experimental framework designed for real-time control, evaluation, and optimization of UAV networks. C2Stack incorporates a modular control plane, referred to as the C2Stack Network Operating System (CNOS), alongside a programmable data plane that exposes APIs for cross-layer algorithm development, digital twin integration, and autonomous swarm control.
papers.title_text: Designing, Deployment and Field Testing of C2Stack for Networked Intelligent Software-Defined UAVs

papers.title: Detecting Liquid Food Adulteration with Mobile Hyperspectral Analysis based on RGB Camera
papers.abstract: Liquid adulteration poses critical societal challenges by endangering public health and causing economic losses. Existing methods on mobile devices rely solely on vibration-based solutions, which face practical limitations due to requirements of specific container materials/structures and vibrational contact. In this paper, we present LiquidLens, a practical, non-contact mobile system for detecting liquid adulteration based on RGB images of liquid surfaces. Inspired by hyperspectral reconstruction, we aim to analyze liquid food's hyperspectral properties from RGB data for effective adulteration detection. To achieve this, we address three major challenges: First, the specular reflections of liquid, which act as a mirror image of surrounding obstacles, distort spectral measurements. Second, the camera's spectral range is restricted to the visible domain, which lacks access to vital information in the invisible bands. Third, the target liquid spectrum is entangled with uncertain ambient illumination, rendering it uninterpretable. To overcome these challenges, we first exploit the camera flash as visible light source and validate its spectral consistency across mobile devices. Next, we design a specular noise suppression technique to cancel the specular noise. Then, we design an RGB-based VIS-NIR spectral recovery (RVN-SR) framework to overcome the spectral range limitation. Besides, a cross-spectral training scheme is designed to train the RVN-SR model in the flash domain, compensating for the lack of NIR radiation. We deploy and validate LiquidLens across multiple smartphones. Experimental results show robust detection accuracy of 96.2% for 8 honey adulteration types and 94.0% for 5 wine adulteration types.
papers.title_text: Detecting Liquid Food Adulteration with Mobile Hyperspectral Analysis based on RGB Camera

papers.title: Direct-to-Cell Satellite Radio Signal Traceback at Scale
papers.abstract: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites borrow licensed RF bands from terrestrial cellular networks to connect our phones anytime, everywhere. However, this spectrum sharing may introduce unexpected satellite RF signals into licensed bands, leading to interference across satellite and terrestrial networks. A prerequisite for addressing these issues is to trace which DtC satellite transmits these radio signals. However, our real-world measurements reveal that this basic task encounters three challenges unique to DtC satellites: inaccurate tracing after their RF pre-compensation for optimization, exhausting tracing to satellite mobility, and incomplete tracing due to dedicated monitoring systems' low coverage and high cost. We devise SatMon, a community-driven backtracer of DtC satellite RF signals at scale. Upon detecting signals of interest, SatMon traces their originating satellites by sensing their cross-user uplink synchronization under orbital constraints. This fingerprint is accurate despite signal pre-compensations. It is deployable not only on existing dedicated monitoring systems but also on ubiquitous regular phones. It also needs only sparse monitors and their existing measurements for wide-area, timely satellite signal tracing at low cost. SatMon has been released to the community and tested in 5 countries. Our real-world field tests and data-driven emulations using 203 million signaling records show that SatMon can identify DtC satellite transmitters at 96.7% accuracy using only two phones at low cost and is robust to radio interference.
papers.title_text: Direct-to-Cell Satellite Radio Signal Traceback at Scale

papers.title: DynaFilter: Cloud-Driven Dynamic Filtering for Satellite Edge Intelligence
papers.abstract: Modern satellite edge systems, including those performing remote sensing tasks such object detection and tracking, are characterized by severely limited bandwidth and intermittent connections, making continuous data transmission to the cloud impractical. Existing edge-cloud systems, however, either require heavy pre-processing before analysis, for instance, full decompression of imagery data, or transmit all compressed data regardless of relevance. To address these challenges, we design DynaFilter, a dynamic filtering technique that enables satellite edge devices to perform selective region-of-interest (RoI) inference directly in the compressed-domain, without full decompression. Our key insight is that low-level compression syntax, specifically DC coefficients/AC energy in JPEG images and motion vectors in video streams, exhibits strong correlations with high-level semantic queries. By establishing a precise mapping between cloud query semantics and multimodal compressed-domain features, DynaFilter enables the edge to identify and transmit only relevant data associated to RoIs. Extensive evaluations show that DynaFilter reduces the total volume of pixel data for decoding and subsequent inference by 1.6×~7.1× for images, and achieves 92.0% bandwidth savings for video streams compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Furthermore, it decreases energy consumption by 43.1~88.6% on target devices and achieves a 1.6×~3.0× speedup in inference latency.
papers.title_text: DynaFilter: Cloud-Driven Dynamic Filtering for Satellite Edge Intelligence

papers.title: ExoMem: OS-Governed Memory for Local Large-LLM Inference on Mobile Edge Devices
papers.abstract: High-quality large language model inference is increasingly used on mobile edge, from satellites to smart homes, where limited connectivity or privacy requirements motivate local model inference. In many such settings, token generation is inherently compute-limited and added latency may be acceptable, but output quality, memory feasibility and crash-free execution are essential. However, on today's mobile edge with unified-memory architectures, running a large model near the device limit can trigger non-deterministic out-of-memory failures. This is because deep learning frameworks retain freed buffers inside caching pools, thus continuing to occupy shared DRAM, which the OS cannot reclaim. During inference, fragmentation and conservative reuse can produce growing memory usage, eventually exceeding the memory availability. In this paper, we present ExoMem, an OS-governed middleware that restores OS authority over physical pages without sacrificing framework compatibility. ExoMem keeps model topology and operators in the framework, while anchoring weights in OS-managed mappings, and introduces a dormant state, whose virtual addresses remain stable for correctness but whose physical pages are immediately reclaimable when needed, leveraging standard OS page caching as an implicit multi-tier hierarchy. Implemented as a plug-and-play extension, ExoMem enables stable local inference for substantially larger LLMs on mobile edge, including 72B-class models on 64GB NVIDIA Jetson devices, while preserving headroom for concurrent workloads.
papers.title_text: ExoMem: OS-Governed Memory for Local Large-LLM Inference on Mobile Edge Devices

papers.title: Experience: Agentic Security Analysis of 5G Protocol Interactions
papers.abstract: This paper reports our three-year experience building 5GAudit, an LLM-based agentic framework for discovering vulnerabilities in 5G protocol interactions. We review the evolution of 5GAudit through successive redesigns, each driven by fundamental deficiencies uncovered in real deployment. We refine 5GAudit to enable it to conduct agentic cross-protocol/domain/system analysis, perform automatic verifier-in-the-loop validations of vulnerabilities, and go beyond predefined threat models by leveraging CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration) theory to enumerate new vulnerability patterns. Our system successfully discovers 42 0-day vulnerabilities of 5G protocol interactions in open-source 5G software, 20 of which have been assigned CVE numbers to date. We demonstrate 5GAudit as an example to share our lessons learned on applying LLM-based agents to 5G-specific security analysis with the community.
papers.title_text: Experience: Agentic Security Analysis of 5G Protocol Interactions

papers.title: Experience: Unveiling GNSS-RTK in the Wild: A 2.5-Year Nationwide Study via Last-Mile Delivery
papers.abstract: GNSS-Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) is designed to deliver precise GNSS positioning, yet its in-the-wild performance on smartphones (i.e., accessibility, precision, and utility) remains unknown. We present the first nationwide, in-the-wild measurement of GNSS-RTK, conducted over 2.5 years across 370 cities in China. Specifically, we leverage the operational processes of JD Logistics, a leading Chinese delivery company serving over 500 million customers, to enable nationwide GNSS-RTK measurement at scale. During daily operations, delivery couriers routinely traverse different areas with smartphones for positioning, enabling low-cost GNSS-RTK data collection at scale. The collected data provides extensive spatio-temporal coverage and repeated sampling, providing a unique opportunity for comprehensive GNSS-RTK performance measurement. Our large-scale measurement reveals that RTK achieves 92.3% overall accessibility, improves precision by 0.95 m over standalone GNSS, and yields an estimated $1.37M in recurring annual benefits from anomaly delivery detection and delivery distance measurement, together with $1.2M in one-time benefits from address coordinate mining.
papers.title_text: Experience: Unveiling GNSS-RTK in the Wild: A 2.5-Year Nationwide Study via Last-Mile Delivery

papers.title: Exploring the Feasibility of Full-Body Muscle Activation Sensing with Insole Pressure Sensors
papers.abstract: Muscle activation initiates contractions that drive human movement, and understanding it provides valuable insights for injury prevention and rehabilitation. Yet, sensing muscle activation is barely explored in the rapidly growing mobile health market. Traditional methods for muscle activation sensing rely on specialized electrodes, such as surface electromyography, making them impractical, especially for long-term usage. In this paper, we introduce Press2Muscle, the first system to unobtrusively infer muscle activation using insole pressure sensors. The key idea is to analyze foot pressure changes resulting from full-body muscle activation that drives movements. To handle variations in pressure signals due to differences in users' gait, weight, and movement styles, we propose a data-driven approach to dynamically adjust reliance on different foot regions and incorporate easily accessible biographical data to enhance Press2Muscle's generalization to unseen users. We conducted an extensive study with 30 users. Under a leave-one-user-out setting, Press2Muscle achieves a root mean square error of 0.025, marking a 19% improvement over a video-based counterpart. A robustness study validates Press2Muscle's ability to generalize across user demographics, footwear types, and walking surfaces. Additionally, we showcase muscle imbalance detection and muscle activation estimation under free-living settings with Press2Muscle, confirming the feasibility of muscle activation sensing using insole pressure sensors in real-world settings.
papers.title_text: Exploring the Feasibility of Full-Body Muscle Activation Sensing with Insole Pressure Sensors

papers.title: General Speech Reconstruction for Voice Calls Using Smartphone's Built-in Accelerometer
papers.abstract: Voice calls are a critical communication mode of interpersonal interaction. However, one of its most significant limitations is susceptibility to ambient noise interference. Current approaches to mitigate noise typically rely on advanced algorithmic processing or supplementary modal signals to enhance the original speech. Nevertheless, when environmental noise reduces the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the original speech below a certain threshold, these methods become entirely ineffective. In this paper, we propose AccVoice, a novel approach that relies solely on the smartphone's builtin accelerometer to capture facial vibration signals, enabling a general speech reconstruction system for voice calls. We first propose a triaxial fusion method to eliminate variations in accelerometer data caused by user-induced micro-motion noise and enhance the feature representation of the signal. Then, we introduce for the first time, to the best of our knowledge, the concept of removing voice timbre to enable cross-user general speech reconstruction capabilities of accelerometer signals. Finally, by employing a large-scale pre-trained speech model combined with a spectrum-separation-based reconstruction approach, we achieve high-quality speech generation. Besides, we use the one-shot sample to re-infuse the timbre into the reconstructed speech to maintain the authenticity of voice calls. We conduct extensive experiments in a cross-user scenario. The results demonstrate that AccVoice achieves high-quality speech reconstruction across different impact factors.
papers.title_text: General Speech Reconstruction for Voice Calls Using Smartphone's Built-in Accelerometer

papers.title: Golden Sniffer: Low-Complexity 5G New Radio Signal Interception Exploiting Gold Sequences
papers.abstract: Sniffing 5G New Radio (NR) transmissions presents a significantly greater challenge compared to LTE, primarily due to the concealment of Radio Network Temporary Identifiers and relevant scrambling parameters. Existing techniques rely on exhaustive searches and simplifying assumptions that often do not hold in real deployments. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different approach that exploits the linearity and non-cryptographic nature of the Gold sequences used in 5G NR for scrambling, drastically reducing the sniffer parameter space to a handful of test alternatives. We also propose and assess a countermeasure that disrupts the phase-based demodulation reference signal reconstruction used by our approach, with only minor impact on legitimate users.
papers.title_text: Golden Sniffer: Low-Complexity 5G New Radio Signal Interception Exploiting Gold Sequences

papers.title: GRADE: Single-Frame Generative Radar Depth Estimation Under Visual Degradation
papers.abstract: Dense 3D depth perception fails under smoke, fog, and darkness because optical sensors cannot penetrate airborne particulates. mmWave radar remains usable and measures range accurately under these conditions, but its small aperture limits angular resolution. We present GRADE, which grounds a pretrained generative prior in single-frame radar geometry to estimate high-fidelity metric depth. GRADE first maps raw 4D radar spectra to coarse metric depth. A latent diffusion backbone then recovers structural detail while conditioning every denoising step on this estimate. A pixel-space adapter uses residual camera cues when available and is trained across clear, smoke-degraded, and occluded inputs so the full output approaches the radar-conditioned path as visibility degrades. Trained and evaluated on ~95K frames across 12 buildings with real smoke, GRADE achieves an MAE of 0.303 m in clear scenes and 0.313 m under smoke, outperforming existing baselines. Code and datasets are available at https://phi-lab-rice.github.io/GRADE.
papers.title_text: GRADE: Single-Frame Generative Radar Depth Estimation Under Visual Degradation

papers.title: Group-Shared Low-Rank Approximation for Mobile-Efficient Pointwise Convolutions in Large-Kernel CNNs
papers.abstract: Large-kernel Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) deliver remarkable performance in vision tasks by significantly expanding receptive fields, yet their quadratic parameter growth critically impedes storage-efficient edge deployment. While existing efficient architectures adopt parameter-efficient depthwise separable convolution backbones that leverage techniques like low-rank approximation and weight sharing to compress depthwise convolutions, we identify a critical oversight: pointwise convolutions dominate parameter volume (>87% in models like RepLKNet-31B) and constitute the primary deployment bottleneck on resource-constrained edge devices. This results in prohibitive storage costs and severe memory-loading constraints on resource-limited devices (e.g., smartphones with 4–12 GB Random Access Memory (RAM)). To overcome this, we propose Channel Group-Shared (CGS) low-rank approximation, a novel Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based parameter-sharing strategy. CGS constructs a structured low-rank paradigm isomorphic to SVD decomposition, comprising shared (high-parameter-cost) down/up-projection matrices across channel groups within a layer and channel-group-specific (low-parameter-cost) scalable diagonal matrices. This group-sharing design achieves significant parameter reduction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that large-kernel CNNs (RepLKNet, ConvNeXt, SLaK) enhanced with CGS strike an empirically favorable balance between competitive performance and substantially reduced storage costs. Crucially, by alleviating storage constraints, reducing memory bandwidth pressure during loading, and minimizing model loading latency, CGS enables the feasible deployment of pre-trained large-kernel CNN models on edge devices, thereby bridging the gap between high-performance vision models and practical edge deployment.
papers.title_text: Group-Shared Low-Rank Approximation for Mobile-Efficient Pointwise Convolutions in Large-Kernel CNNs

papers.title: Hark: Breaking Receiver Power Limits of LoRa
papers.abstract: A long-standing challenge for LoRa devices has been to enable ultra-low-power reception that supports always-on listening while preserving the standard LoRa PHY and compatibility with existing COTS transmitters. Currently, COTS LoRa radios fail to support spontaneous actuation due to the prohibitive receive power (~43.5 mW) required to listen continuously, which effectively locks out applications that fall under LoRaWAN Class C. Recent works achieve substantially lower receive power, but either require modified physical layers and coordinated helper transmissions, or forgo dechirping and the range it provides. To this end, we present Hark, an ultra-low-power LoRa receiver that enables always-on listening at 1.90 mW while fully demodulating and decoding standard frames from unmodified COTS transmitters. We achieve this by pairing a novel digital wake-up pipeline with an analog tunnel-diode oscillator frontend that exhibits autodyning and is disciplined by a shared, unsynchronized, unmodulated carrier emitter. Specifically, Hark samples the channel at a fraction of the Nyquist rate to minimize compute and ADC power, yet successfully demodulates standard LoRa frames even below the noise floor. Hark demonstrates a communication range of nearly 500 m while still reducing receive power by over 22× compared to the COTS LoRa receiver. Hark therefore targets deployments where standard LoRa transmitters must remain unmodified and a receiver-side carrier emitter can be shared across multiple receivers.
papers.title_text: Hark: Breaking Receiver Power Limits of LoRa

papers.title: InstMeter: An Instruction-Level Method to Predict Energy and Latency of DL Model Inference on MCUs
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) models can now run on microcontrollers (MCUs). Through neural architecture search (NAS), we can search DL models that meet the constraints of MCUs. Among various constraints, energy and latency costs of the model inference are critical metrics. To predict them, existing research relies on coarse proxies such as multiply-accumulations (MACs) and model's input parameters, often resulting in inaccurate predictions or requiring extensive data collection. In this paper, we propose InstMeter, a predictor leveraging MCUs' clock cycles to accurately estimate the energy and latency of DL models. Clock cycles are fundamental metrics reflecting MCU operations, directly determining energy and latency costs. Furthermore, a unique property of our predictor is its strong linearity, allowing it to be simple and accurate. We thoroughly evaluate InstMeter under different scenarios, MCUs, and software settings. Compared with state-of-the-art studies, InstMeter can reduce the energy and latency prediction errors by 3× and 6.5×, respectively, while requiring 100× and 10× less training data. In the NAS scenario, InstMeter can fully exploit the energy budget, identifying optimal DL models with higher inference accuracy. We also evaluate InstMeter's generalization performance through various experiments on three ARM MCUs (Cortex-M4, M7, M33) and one RISC-V-based MCU (ESP32-C3), different compilation options (-Os, -O2), GCC versions (v7.3, v10.3), application scenarios (keyword spotting, image recognition), dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, temperatures (21°C, 43°C), and software settings (TFLMv2.4, TFLMvCI). Our source codes and the MCU-specific benchmark datasets are available here: https://github.com/haoliu001/InstMeter.
papers.title_text: InstMeter: An Instruction-Level Method to Predict Energy and Latency of DL Model Inference on MCUs

papers.title: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference
papers.abstract: On-device LLM inference is attractive for privacy and responsiveness, but remains challenging on mobile and embedded devices because model weights far exceed available DRAM. Prior systems exploit activation sparsity and offload weights to SSD or flash storage, but face a fundamental systems tradeoff: accurate sparse execution decisions require the latest context, whereas efficient computation-I/O overlap requires early prediction. As a result, existing designs either serialize execution or incur redundant weight fetches, extra computation, and large cache overheads. We present LeanStream, a streaming speculate-and-refine framework for efficient on-device LLM inference. LeanStream progressively refines computation, loading, and cache-retention priorities using partial GPU results, enabling fine-grained overlap between GPU execution and storage I/O. We implement LeanStream on both mobile and embedded platforms. Compared with prior on-device LLM inference systems, LeanStream reduces memory usage by 4.8×-7.5× at the best throughput achieved by prior work, while further improving token generation throughput by 1.6×-2.1×.
papers.title_text: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference

papers.title: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
papers.abstract: Mobile advertising dominates app monetization but introduces risks ranging from intrusive user experience to malware delivery. Existing detection methods rely either on static analysis, which misses runtime behaviors, or on heuristic UI exploration, which struggles with sparse and obfuscated ads. In this paper, we present MANA, the first agentic multimodal reasoning framework for mobile ad detection. MANA integrates static, visual, temporal, and experiential signals into a reasoning-guided navigation strategy that determines not only how to traverse interfaces but also where to focus, enabling efficient and robust exploration. We implement and evaluate MANA on commercial smartphones over 200 apps, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency. Compared to baselines, it improves detection accuracy by 30.5%-56.3% and reduces exploration steps by 29.7%-63.3%. Case studies further demonstrate its ability to uncover obfuscated and malicious ads, underscoring its practicality for mobile ad auditing and its potential for broader runtime UI analysis (e.g., permission abuse). Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/MANA-2026/MANA.
papers.title_text: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation

papers.title: Mechanically Programmable Reflective Metasurfaces: A General Low‑Cost Paradigm for High‑Frequency Wavefront Control
papers.abstract: Programmable reflective metasurfaces enable flexible wave manipulation, but conventional resonance-based designs suffer from high cost, narrow bandwidth, complex calibration, and limited deployability at high frequencies. We present MetaX, a low-cost mechanically programmable metasurface that controls wavefronts by continuously deforming a reflective membrane with only 64 micro-motors. Geometric path-length modulation enables broadband, calibration-free operation across different wave domains. We further develop a differentiable model that maps actuator commands to 3D surface deformation and wave responses, and use gradient-based inverse design to generate mechanical code-books for wide-angle single-beam steering and concurrent multi-beam generation. Experiments with a 64-actuator prototype demonstrate stable RF beam steering over 77-81 GHz with a maximum frequency-induced pointing deviation of only 2.5° and support for four concurrent beams with at most 1.07 dB average inter-user power imbalance. The experiments further demonstrate that adjusting the motor spacing enables the MetaX prototype to support beam steering across other frequency bands within 20-85 GHz. The complete prototype costs approximately $81, demonstrating low-cost, broadband, and multi-beam wavefront control for high frequencies.
papers.title_text: Mechanically Programmable Reflective Metasurfaces: A General Low‑Cost Paradigm for High‑Frequency Wavefront Control

papers.title: MetaVenom: Field Programmable Fully Passive Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Emerging high frequency wireless sensing and communication systems often leverage metasurfaces to modulate the signal propagation, thereby transcending Snell's law. Yet, existing metasurfaces are either active, which is constantly sustained by electrical power, or passive, which cannot be reconfigured. In this paper, we explore a quasi-dynamic meta-surface using electrically morphable ferrofluid that enables a new category of metasurface design for wireless sensing and communication. We first characterize how ferrofluid material interact with high-frequency millimeter-wave signals. Next, we present a practical fabrication method of quasi-dynamic metasurface using thermoplastic 3D printing. We then develop a model to effectively manipulate the wireless signal propagation using an array of field-programmable ferrofluid cells. Our extensive evaluation results reveal the capabilities of a novel quasi-dynamic metasurface as an alternative to existing wireless tags for joint radar communication, and beamforming metasurfaces for enhancing millimeter-wave network coverage.
papers.title_text: MetaVenom: Field Programmable Fully Passive Metasurfaces

papers.title: MetaVision: Enhancing Resolution for Wi-Fi Vision with Hierarchical Programmable Metasurface
papers.abstract: Wi-Fi has emerged as a promising medium for device-free human sensing, yet its capability in fine-grained sensing tasks remains rather limited. In particular, existing solutions to human pose estimation (HPE) demand extensive hardware elevations (e.g., multiple antennas or transceivers) directly upon Wi-Fi home deployments, typically involving very few APs and clients. In this paper, we present MetaVision, a system that utilizes programmable metasurfaces as external add-on to create multiple virtual viewpoints, thus substantially extending the spatial diversity of a single pair of AP and client. MetaVision organizes its metasurfaces into a master-slave hierarchy to tackle inter-surfaces synchronization. It further separates individual signals from these homogeneous metasurfaces, exploiting a novel temporal encoding scheme that effectively decouples superimposed signals into independent signal spectrograms. Fusing these multi-view spectral representations, MetaVision employs a neural network to model inter-joint dependencies and to accordingly reconstruct 3D human poses. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MetaVision achieves high-resolution 3D HPE and reduces error by 61% compared with baseline approaches.
papers.title_text: MetaVision: Enhancing Resolution for Wi-Fi Vision with Hierarchical Programmable Metasurface

papers.title: mmFHE: mmWave Sensing with End-to-End Fully Homomorphic Encryption
papers.abstract: We present mmFHE, the first system that executes the entire cloud-side mmWave sensing pipeline including the DSP and ML inference under fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). mmFHE encrypts range profiles on an edge device after lightweight plaintext preprocessing and executes the entire mmWave signal-processing and ML inference pipeline homomorphically on a semi-honest cloud that operates exclusively on ciphertexts. At the core of mmFHE is a library of seven composable, data-oblivious FHE kernels that replace standard DSP routines with fixed arithmetic circuits for different application-specific pipelines. We demonstrate this approach on two representative tasks: vital-sign monitoring and gesture recognition. We formally prove two cryptographic guarantees for any pipeline assembled from this library: input privacy and data obliviousness. These guarantees effectively neutralize various supervised and unsupervised privacy attacks on raw data, including re-identification and data-dependent privacy leakage. Evaluation on three public radar datasets shows that encryption introduces negligible error versus the plaintext pipeline, with 84.5% gesture accuracy (vs. 84.7%). End-to-end cloud GPU latency is 1.21 s per 10 s vital-sign window and 5.76 s per 3 s gesture window. These results establish the initial feasibility of end-to-end mmWave sensing under FHE on commodity hardware.
papers.title_text: mmFHE: mmWave Sensing with End-to-End Fully Homomorphic Encryption

papers.title: MoiréSkin: Ultra-Sensitive Sensor–Actuator Visuo-Tactile Skin using Moiré Patterns
papers.abstract: Robots increasingly must perform dexterous object manipulation in real-world environments, yet existing VTS offer rich camera-based spatial readout while rigid optics limit force sensitivity, force range, and active compliance regulation. We present MoiréSkin, an inflatable visuo-tactile skin using flexible Moiré optics to unify ultra-sensitive tactile sensing and active compliance regulation. Dual-sided submillimeter gratings in a soft membrane amplify microscopic contact-induced strain into large, high-contrast Moiré fringe variations for tactile readout. To balance reliability and sensitivity, our tailored soft-material grating pipeline combines internal illumination with fluorescent doping to suppress ambient-light interference. Self-supervised calibration compensates for air-pressure-dependent sensing drift during pneumatic regulation, while a neural pipeline uses pre- and post-contact fringes to estimate contact position and force. Experiments show that MoiréSkin achieves 0.094 mm position and 0.0038 N contact force MAE, outperforming prior VTS by an order of magnitude. It also reaches 99.7% 10-shot classification accuracy over 7 ultra-soft materials spanning 8.73–21.72 kPa Young's modulus, and measures shear-force-related liquid mass variation with ~4 g precision, demonstrating a new path toward ultra-sensitive sensor-actuator visuo-tactile skins.
papers.title_text: MoiréSkin: Ultra-Sensitive Sensor–Actuator Visuo-Tactile Skin using Moiré Patterns

papers.title: Monitoring Electrical Transformer Mechanics via Crowdsourced Imaging
papers.abstract: Electrical transformers are critical to power grids, and their mechanical integrity directly impacts system stability. Existing monitoring approaches, such as accelerometer, acoustic, and piezoelectric sensing, require intrusive installation and are often costly or impractical for real-time assessment. To overcome these limitations, we propose Transcope, a computational imaging framework that remotely infers transformer mechanical states by analyzing the illumination variations of a transformer-connected bulb. The key principle is vibration-to-flicker coupling, where abnormal mechanical states induce voltage ripples that modulate bulb brightness and create a visual proxy for internal vibrations. To this end, we develop a flicker-aware physical model to characterize the mapping from bulb images to flicker signals, and further design a diffusion-based framework to reconstruct vibration signals from weak visual observations. Extensive experiments on a real-world testbed with more than 100k samples show that Transcope achieves 0.070 MAE and 19.08 dB SNR in vibration reconstruction, and reaches 98.79% accuracy and 96.19% macro F1-score in anomaly diagnosis. These results demonstrate the promise of reliable, non-contact transformer monitoring using ordinary cameras.
papers.title_text: Monitoring Electrical Transformer Mechanics via Crowdsourced Imaging

papers.title: MORSE: Multipath Resilient One-Shot Localization for RIS via Spatial Spectral Encoding
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) offer a promising way to control wireless propagation by engineering reflected paths. However, realizing this vision requires real-time knowledge of users' location relative to the RIS. This is challenging because RIS lack the capability to sense the channel, while existing approaches rely on beam search with high overhead. This paper presents MORSE, a novel one-shot localization framework that leverages the inherent frequency-dependent radiation patterns of RIS to create spatial-spectral encoding, where each spatial direction corresponds to a unique spectral signature. A user can then infer its angular position relative to the RIS by observing the received power spectrum. To ensure robustness in multipath environments, MORSE excites the RIS using an FMCW chirp, allowing the receiver to separate propagation paths by delay and isolate the spectral signature of the direct RIS-UE path. We implement MORSE on a 12×12 RIS prototype operating from 3 to 6 GHz and evaluate it through extensive over-the-air experiments in three environments. Our results demonstrate accurate single-shot joint azimuth and elevation angle estimation and robustness to multipath interference, enabling RIS adaptation in dynamic wireless environments.
papers.title_text: MORSE: Multipath Resilient One-Shot Localization for RIS via Spatial Spectral Encoding

papers.title: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking
papers.abstract: On-device mobile Large Language Model (LLM) inference is gaining significant attention. However, mobile devices operate in highly dynamic multitasking environments where users frequently switch between applications. This creates memory pressure, forcing LLM memory—model weights and KV cache—to be evicted by the operating system. When a new inference request arrives, the inference system must restore the evicted memory through slow storage reads or recompute the entire KV cache, severely degrading responsiveness. To address this, we present mzCache, an on-device LLM inference system with specialized memory management for multitasking environments. Under unpredictable memory pressure, mzCache elastically evicts LLM memory and leverages the unified memory of mobile SoCs to enable zero-wait inference on the GPU with concurrent CPU-side restoration. mzCache realizes this through restoration-oriented memory management: LLM memory is partitioned into fine-grained shared buffers to enable partial eviction and restoration with concurrent cross-processor access, while hybrid swap and backward-out eviction policies ensure low-latency restoration from any eviction state. Implemented on llama.cpp and deployed as an Android application, mzCache achieves 2.1–5.5× reduction in Time-to-First-Token compared to storage-backed partial offload and demonstrates its effectiveness in real multitasking scenarios.
papers.title_text: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking

papers.title: Nexus: Efficient and Scalable Multi-Cell mmWave Baseband Processing with Heterogeneous Compute
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of 5G New Radio (NR), particularly in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) spectrum, imposes stringent demands on baseband processing efficiency. While virtualized Radio Access Networks (vRANs) enable dynamic spectrum sharing, compute resource allocation for baseband processing, especially in multi-cell deployments, remains underexplored. In this paper, we present Nexus, the first system to realize real-time, virtualized multi-cell mmWave baseband processing on a single server with heterogeneous compute resources. For single-cell operation, Nexus employs a random forest (RAF)-based model to predict energy-efficient resource allocations with microsecond-level inference latency. For multi-cell scenarios, Nexus introduces a power-aware scheduler that incorporates a lightweight contention model to adapt allocations under concurrent execution. Through extensive evaluations, we show that Nexus supports up to sixteen concurrent cells under full load, achieving 5.37 Gbps aggregate throughput using sixteen CPU cores and a single physical ACC100 accelerator virtualized into sixteen virtual functions (VFs), while reducing the multi-cell scheduling search space by orders of magnitude.
papers.title_text: Nexus: Efficient and Scalable Multi-Cell mmWave Baseband Processing with Heterogeneous Compute

papers.title: nn-Live: Predicting Runtime Latency for Concurrent DNN Inference on Mobile Devices
papers.abstract: Modern mobile applications (e.g., AR/XR, assistant robots) increasingly rely on multiple concurrent DNN models, yet their inference latency becomes highly unpredictable under dynamic resource contention from concurrent workloads. In mobile SoCs with heterogeneous CPU architectures, such as big. LITTLE designs, the latency is affected by a complex interplay of factors, including heterogeneous core performance, cache hierarchies and shared memory bandwidth. Existing latency prediction methods either fail to capture runtime dynamics or overlook the heterogeneity in mobile processors. In this paper, we propose nn-Live that can predict live inference latency for DNN models on mobile CPUs under dynamically changing operating conditions. nn-Live leverages per-core hardware counter statistics to quantify the interference from concurrent tasks, and utilizes a lightweight linear model to estimate each core's interference contribution to a specific task, enabling robust latency prediction across dynamic execution conditions. Given the large pool of DNN models and huge potential task placement configurations, nn-Live further adopts an adaptive hierarchical sampling strategy to reduce profiling cost while preserving configuration diversity and representativeness. We build a large-scale interference analysis dataset1 across three mainstream SoCs. Evaluation results show that nn-Live achieves high prediction accuracy under diverse runtime environments, with a clear advantage over existing methods. We further demonstrate the extensibility of nn-Live to mobile accelerators (e.g., GPU/NPU).
papers.title_text: nn-Live: Predicting Runtime Latency for Concurrent DNN Inference on Mobile Devices

papers.title: NPUGen: NPU as KV Generator for Stable Long-Context Mobile LLM Inference
papers.abstract: As on-device large language model (LLM) applications like mobile agents become increasingly popular, long-context inference has become a key challenge. The key-value (KV) cache is the foundation of efficient autoregressive decoding, but its memory footprint grows rapidly with context length, often exceeding the memory limits of mobile devices. Existing KV cache management methods, such as compression and storage offloading, often lead to performance degradation or unpredictable stall latency. We find that in the prevalent CPU/GPU-decoding mobile pipelines, the NPU remains largely idle during decoding and can recompute missing KV cache more efficiently than storage offloading. We therefore propose NPUGen, whose KV recomputation engine generates missing KV cache on the idle NPU via a prefill-like forward pass, avoiding unstable storage I/O, CPU intervention, and unnecessary data movement. NPUGen further introduces a hidden-state anchor mechanism that eliminates redundant prefix recomputation, and turns KV recomputation into a schedulable background service to cope with resource contention and guarantee foreground QoS. Experiments on smartphones with Qualcomm SoCs across multiple long-context tasks show that NPUGen significantly reduces decoding latency and fluctuations, providing fast and stable long-context inference on resource-constrained mobile devices.
papers.title_text: NPUGen: NPU as KV Generator for Stable Long-Context Mobile LLM Inference

papers.title: OrbWeaver : A Geometric Optics-Based RIS for Omnidirectional 3D Beam Steering
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) are a key 6G technology for controlling the wireless environment and eliminating signal blockages. However, dominant planar meta-surfaces suffer from high cost, complex control, limited 3D coverage, and high beam alignment overhead. This paper presents OrbWeaver, an RIS that replaces complex metasurfaces with a 3D-printed Luneburg lens and a simple reconfigurable RF switching fabric. It leverages geometric optics for cost-effective, programmable signal redirection across an omnidirectional 3D field of view. A key advantage is its ability to perform in-situ power measurements, enabling a decoupled beam alignment protocol that drastically simplifies multi-node coordination. We validate OrbWeaver with mmWave and sub-6 GHz prototypes, demonstrating its frequency-agnostic design. In real-world 5G and Wi-Fi deployments, OrbWeaver eliminates dead zones, achieving throughput gains up to 430 Mbps and 241 Mbps, respectively. Our results establish OrbWeaver as a practical RIS solution to overcome the deployment barriers of conventional metasurfaces.
papers.title_text: OrbWeaver : A Geometric Optics-Based RIS for Omnidirectional 3D Beam Steering

papers.title: ORNet: OFDMA-Enabled mmWave Radar ISAC Networks
papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar backscatter communication (RBC) is an emerging Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) paradigm that combines high-resolution sensing with low-power connectivity. However, existing systems rely on frequency modulation or coarse frequency-division multiplexing, forcing each tag to occupy the full frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) bandwidth or sacrifice data rate for concurrency, which fundamentally limits scalability. This raises a key question: can radar-centric RBC systems support OFDMA-like multi-user access?
papers.title_text: ORNet: OFDMA-Enabled mmWave Radar ISAC Networks

papers.title: PassiveOFDM: Flexible OFDM Backscatter with Commercial Compatibility
papers.abstract: To enable commercial-compatible Wi-Fi backscatter transmission, recent works either adopt off-tag mechanisms based on standard OFDM Wi-Fi exciters, or generate OFDM Wi-Fi waveforms on-tag using single-tone exciter. However, they result in either very limited communication range or exorbitant power consumption. We present PassiveOFDM, the first μW-level commercial-compatible OFDM Wi-Fi backscatter system that works at tens of meters exciter-to-tag distance. It enables low-power on-tag OFDM signal forming, decoupling tag placement from the exciter's location. We design a spectrum-filling shaping scheme that retains the spectrum structure of the OFDM Wi-Fi without IFFT, and a DAC-free waveform embedding scheme with low-power RF switches. Our field tests confirm that PassiveOFDM achieves reliable backscatter transmission 65m from the exciter or 80m from the receiver. Its power consumption is 2855.1× smaller than the SOTA on-tag system RF-Transformer. Its exciter-to-tag distance and throughput are 54.2× and 29× higher than those of the SOTA off-tag system TiScatter, respectively.
papers.title_text: PassiveOFDM: Flexible OFDM Backscatter with Commercial Compatibility

papers.title: PathClean: Breaking the Multipath Barrier for High-Fidelity mmWave Human Point Clouds
papers.abstract: High-fidelity mmWave human point clouds are pivotal for applications like fall detection, people counting, and multi-person pose estimation. However, commercial radars are often hindered by multipath interference in cluttered indoor environments, which introduces ghost targets and distorts human structures. Prior attempts at mitigation either rely on temporal continuity, environmental priors, or data-hungry learning models, all of which suffer from latency, fragility, or high overhead. We present PathClean, the first system to eliminate multipath interference directly during point cloud generation instead of post-processing. PathClean leverages the inherent Angle of Arrival (AoA)-Angle of Departure (AoD) consistency of direct paths to instantly suppress multipath, while addressing the challenges of dense matching ambiguity, hardware imperfections, and real-time constraints. Implemented on commodity radars, PathClean removes 98.9% of multipath points, while retaining 97.6% of true human points. Extensive experiments across seven environments and three case studies—fall detection, people counting, and multi-person pose estimation—demonstrate that PathClean is robust, scalable, and practical for real-world deployment.
papers.title_text: PathClean: Breaking the Multipath Barrier for High-Fidelity mmWave Human Point Clouds

papers.title: PATHS: Plug-and-Play Tracking from Heterogeneous Streams to a Shared Token Interface
papers.abstract: Multimodal target tracking estimates a moving target's trajectory by fusing heterogeneous per-anchor feature streams from sensing modalities. Existing tracking pipelines are usually built for a fixed feature set and anchor layout. They become brittle when streams drop out, new feature families are introduced, or the deployment changes. We present PATHS, a deployment-aware token interface for plug-and-play tracking. PATHS converts per-anchor feature streams into a shared, fixed-width token interface, allowing a unified tracking model to operate as the available feature mix changes. To add a feature family, PATHS trains only a new encoder with a frozen reference decoder, aligning its tokens to the shared interface without paired cross-modal data. At runtime, set attention fuses any available tokens, and a shared decoder reconstructs the trajectory. A reference-frame mapping adapts PATHS to different spatial scales without retraining. Across seven feature families in simulation and three real deployments, PATHS achieves mean tracking errors of 0.13–0.49 m and reduces median error by up to 33% relative to fixed-input baselines under stream quality fluctuations.
papers.title_text: PATHS: Plug-and-Play Tracking from Heterogeneous Streams to a Shared Token Interface

papers.title: Prism: Efficient Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning for On-Device LLMs
papers.abstract: On-device fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs) is becoming increasingly important for personalized AI assistants and adaptive agents. However, standard backpropagation imposes substantial training-state memory overheads that often exceed the stringent resource budgets of mobile platforms. To address this, Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization leverages forward-only probing instead of backpropagation, drastically reducing memory footprints and offering a compelling alternative for on-device adaptation. Nonetheless, scaling ZO fine-tuning to billion-scale trainable parameter spaces remains challenging, as the cost of recovering reliable update directions scales poorly with dimensionality under mobile constraints. In this paper, we present Prism, a mobile-native infrastructure for practical billion-scale on-device ZO fine-tuning. Prism re-architects the ZO loop around a scalable probing substrate, bringing both per-step training latency and memory overhead closer to the inference footprint. We implement Prism end to end on commodity smartphones and evaluate it across diverse tasks and multiple model scales. Prism achieves accuracy comparable to that of state-of-the-art ZO fine-tuning baselines while reducing per-step latency by 53.4%-76.3% and peak memory by 10.6%-13.8% relative to the best baseline in each setting. These results demonstrate the practical feasibility of billion-scale on-device ZO fine-tuning for LLMs under real mobile constraints. We will release our code to support future research.
papers.title_text: Prism: Efficient Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning for On-Device LLMs

papers.title: RadioSight: Predictive mmWave XR Network Optimization from Dynamic Neural Radio Fields
papers.abstract: Next-generation extended reality (XR) networks rely on mmWave communication for multi-gigabit throughput, yet highly directional links are vulnerable to user mobility and blockages, causing frequent outages under reactive beam management. Emerging neural radio fields can predict radio propagation, but prior work remains limited to offline channel reconstruction. We introduce RadioSight, a real-time multi-modal radio field system for predictive mmWave optimization and proactive Multi-User MIMO beamforming. RadioSight combines backward beam-tracing with real-time semantic object synchronization to anticipate RF geometry changes without full model retraining. Implemented as an edge-executable pipeline for commercial 28 GHz arrays, RadioSight determines each scheduling window's beams during the preceding window without exhaustive beam sweeps. Experiments show that RadioSight reduces beam-search error by up to ~50%, improves median throughput by 2×, and enhances link stability.
