papers.title: RadioStream: A Wideband Multi-Antenna SDR Platform
papers.abstract: Software-defined radios are central to wireless systems research, but their host-centric streaming interfaces grow fragile exactly where modern experiments push hardest: wide bandwidth, many antennas, and fine slot-level control. The root difficulty is a timing-domain mismatch: the FPGA and RF front-end run on a deterministic, sample-clock-driven timeline, while the host operates asynchronously under operating-system scheduling, and traditional stacks resolve this by forcing the host to keep pace with the radio, producing late packets, underflows, and overflows at wideband rates. We present RadioStream, a radio-centric, slot-synchronous SDR architecture that makes the slot, rather than the raw sample stream, the unit of coordination across the host-radio boundary. The FPGA owns slot timing and time-critical radio actions and exports slot boundaries to the host as explicit slot-tick Ethernet packets, while the host runs asynchronously behind slot-aligned buffers over a lightweight fronthaul, with a two-slot look-ahead for control. A DPDK-based host path integrates directly with frameworks such as GNU Radio, Python, and MATLAB. On a 100G interface, RadioStream sustains 90 Gbps concurrently on uplink and downlink with no packet drops, streams 2 GHz of aggregated RF bandwidth, bounds slot-tick jitter below 600 ns at the 99th percentile, and applies per-slot control reaching the RF output in under 500 ns. We demonstrate RadioStream across communication, mmWave beam sweeping, and sub-6 GHz multi-antenna sensing workloads, showing that reliable, high-throughput streaming and deterministic fine-grained control hold together in practice.
papers.title_text: RadioStream: A Wideband Multi-Antenna SDR Platform

papers.title: RF-LEGO: Modularized Signal Processing-Deep Learning Co-Design for RF Sensing via Deep Unrolling
papers.abstract: Wireless sensing, traditionally relying on signal processing (SP) techniques, has recently shifted toward data-driven deep learning (DL) to achieve performance breakthroughs. However, existing deep wireless sensing models are typically end-to-end and task-specific, lacking reusability and interpretability. We propose RF-LEGO, a modular co-design framework that transforms interpretable SP algorithms into trainable, physics-grounded DL modules through deep unrolling. By replacing hand-tuned parameters with learnable ones while preserving core processing structures and mathematical operators, RF-LEGO ensures modularity, cascadability, and structure-aligned interpretability. Specifically, we introduce three deep-unrolled modules for critical RF sensing tasks: frequency transform, spatial angle estimation, and signal detection. Extensive experiments using real-world data for Wi-Fi, millimeter-wave, UWB, and 6G sensing demonstrate that RF-LEGO significantly outperforms existing SP and DL baselines, both standalone and when integrated into multiple downstream tasks. RF-LEGO pioneers a novel SP-DL co-design paradigm for wireless sensing via deep unrolling, shedding light on efficient and interpretable deep wireless sensing solutions. Our code is available at https://github.com/aiot-lab/RF-LEGO.
papers.title_text: RF-LEGO: Modularized Signal Processing-Deep Learning Co-Design for RF Sensing via Deep Unrolling

papers.title: RF-Tactrix: Fingerprint-Inspired Battery-Free, Wireless Force Sensing And Localization on 2D Surfaces
papers.abstract: Accurate sensing and localization of surface force are crucial in various applications, including muscle rehabilitation, robotic manipulation of fragile objects, and finger rehabilitation training. However, existing technologies struggle to achieve high-precision and continuous force sensing, due to the crosstalk interference from dense sensor arrays or ambient light interference from optical sensors or reliance on batteries and power-hungry components.
papers.title_text: RF-Tactrix: Fingerprint-Inspired Battery-Free, Wireless Force Sensing And Localization on 2D Surfaces

papers.title: RollingPol: Single-Shot Polarization Imaging for Underwater Sensing
papers.abstract: Underwater optical sensing is severely degraded by backscattered light from suspended particles. While polarization-based image enhancement methods can suppress this backscattering effect, existing methods are either costly, or require sequential image captures that do not handle dynamic scenes. Recently, learning-based enhancement methods have shown promising results, but they depend on large paired datasets that are difficult to obtain underwater and introduce noise or artifacts due to domain gaps.
papers.title_text: RollingPol: Single-Shot Polarization Imaging for Underwater Sensing

papers.title: Shape-Reconfigurable Charger: Magnetic Power Pathway Programming via Computed Morphing
papers.abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) enables contactless power delivery, with magnetic resonance coupling (MRC-WPT) as a leading approach. However, existing MRC-WPT systems rely on fixed transmitter (TX) geometries, limiting their tolerance to receiver (RX) displacement. While circuit-level tuning can improve power flow, it operates within fixed magnetic pathways and cannot reconfigure the field at the source, thus offering limited adaptability. This paper presents Shape-Reconfigurable Charger (SRC), an in-plane MRC-WPT charging system that senses its pose, morphs its structure to optimize power pathways, and adapts its configuration. SRC employs silicone tubes filled with liquid metal (LM) as coils and attaches liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers as tendons, enabling morphable TX coils. We formulate online coil configuration as a dynamic black-box optimization and develop a distributed Bayesian optimization framework that runs on each TX, requiring no RX communication or inter-TX coordination. A hardware prototype demonstrates our performance across diverse RX placements: SRC improves power delivered to load (PDL) by 174% over frequency tuning and 96% over motorized rotation on average. By reframing the TX design as adaptive field shaping, SRC moves MRC-WPT beyond rigid transmission toward programmable magnetic pathways, advancing the vision of truly unconstrained wireless charging.
papers.title_text: Shape-Reconfigurable Charger: Magnetic Power Pathway Programming via Computed Morphing

papers.title: Sparsity-Aware Scheduling for Efficient MoE-Based LLM Serving on Edge Servers
papers.abstract: To support real-time and domain-customized edge intelligent applications, LLMs are increasingly deployed on edge computing servers. However, we observe that current MoE-based LLM serving systems, inherited from the cloud-based architectures, face a critical sparsity-vanishing problem when serving at the edge: tokens within an input batch often activate a large fraction of experts, which incurs significant I/O overhead from frequent expert swapping between CPU and GPU memory, ultimately degrading system throughput. In this work, we propose Saber, a sparsity-aware scheduling framework optimized for efficient MoE-based LLM serving on edge servers. The core idea of Saber is to introduce a group-level batching strategy that dynamically identifies requests with similar activated experts, and coalesces them to construct sparsity-preserving input batches. To ensure efficient online execution, activation patterns are precomputed and clustered offline, enabling fast request grouping through a lightweight classifier at runtime. Additionally, Saber incorporates a utility-driven priority scheduling mechanism to maximize inference throughput while maintaining low latency by intelligently adjusting group priorities. Experiments on representative MoE-based LLMs demonstrate that Saber significantly outperforms existing sparsity-agnostic schedulers, achieving up to 3.8× lower batch execution time and 3.27× higher throughput at comparable latency levels.
papers.title_text: Sparsity-Aware Scheduling for Efficient MoE-Based LLM Serving on Edge Servers

papers.title: Spatially Selective Radar Backscatter Communication
papers.abstract: This paper presents Serena, the first spatially selective radar backscatter communication system that is capable of delivering messages to radars at specific locations. Serena offers a low-power solution for properly delivering location-specific messages (e.g., no-fly-zone alert, speed-reduction warning, turning notification) to radar-equipped vehicles (e.g., automobile, UAV, UGV). Rather than manipulating RF signals with power-intensive components, Serena leverages the limited modulation capability of multiple low-power backscatter tags to generate spatially selective radar signal feature, and further utilizes such signal feature to represent bits. Such design philosophy is primarily realized by our two core designs: (i) a multi-tag distributed and synchronous modulation technique that generates spatially selective radar signal feature (i.e., the combination of the frequencies of tag-generated harmonics in radar IF spectrum); (ii) an intermittent mutual synchronization protocol that achieves 10-μs level inter-tag synchronization under only 10μW-level power consumption. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that Serena achieves desirable spatial selectivity in diverse environments: it achieves less than 1% average BER at target locations, while keeping the average BER around 30% at non-target locations.
papers.title_text: Spatially Selective Radar Backscatter Communication

papers.title: SpatialMind: Spatially Aware On-Device Embodied AI via Viewpoint Integration​
papers.abstract: On-device embodied AI allows local processing of visual data and prompt responses to user requests. Applying embodied AI to more complex domains requires spatial cognition, to properly comprehend the 3D environment and geometric relations between objects. However, existing vision-language models (VLMs) are weak in spatial cognition due to their limitations to 2D image understandings. In this paper, we present SpatialMind, a new on-device embodied AI technique that bridges the gap between 2D visual inputs and 3D physical reality, by injecting 3D spatial knowledge into on-device VLMs in a sparse form of 2D allocentric spatial memory. This memory is constructed by systematically aligning cross-frame visual features to a unified global viewpoint, and we prune the scope of on-device computation to maximize the compute efficiency in memory construction and VLM reasoning. Experiment results in diverse indoor environments show that SpatialMind greatly enhances the performance of spatially aware on-device embodied AI tasks, with high adaptability, robustness and compute efficiency.
papers.title_text: SpatialMind: Spatially Aware On-Device Embodied AI via Viewpoint Integration​

papers.title: SwimHR: Wearable-Free Heart Rate Monitoring for Swimmers via Water-Mediated ECG Sensing
papers.abstract: Heart rate (HR) monitoring during swimming is crucial for athlete performance optimization and physiological assessment. Yet existing solutions remain unsatisfactory. ECG chest straps require tight skin contact and are often uncomfortable during swimming, while photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors suffer severe accuracy degradation due to swimming-induced motion artifacts. We present SwimHR, the first wearable-free HR monitoring system that captures electrocardiogram (ECG) signals transmitted through pool water without any on-body device. To enable practical pool-scale underwater ECG sensing, we (1) derive and validate a physical model of ECG transmission in water and quantify environmental attenuation in swimming pools through simulation, (2) design a lane-scale sensing architecture with a bias-electrode-free acquisition circuit for reliable full-lane coverage, and (3) develop a U-Net-based pipeline for robust R-peak detection under stroke-dependent swimming artifacts. We evaluate SwimHR with 34 swimmers (12 amateur and 22 professional) across four strokes and multiple pools. SwimHR achieves a mean HR error of 1.0 bpm with a standard deviation of 0.9 bpm relative to the ECG ground truth, significantly outperforming PPG-based wearables. SwimHR demonstrates the feasibility of accurate, real-time, wearable-free HR monitoring in standard swimming pool settings while avoiding the discomfort of body-worn sensors.
papers.title_text: SwimHR: Wearable-Free Heart Rate Monitoring for Swimmers via Water-Mediated ECG Sensing

papers.title: TACToC: Enabling Task-Adaptive Communication System with a Task-Describable Encoder
papers.abstract: Task-oriented communications (ToC), also known as semantic communications, offers a promising paradigm for offloading deep neural network (DNN) inference from edge devices to more powerful remote servers. By transmitting only task-specific information, ToC significantly reduces the communication overhead inherent in conventional offloading systems. However, existing ToC approaches exhibit limited task adaptivity, requiring retraining or separate encoders for each task—hindering their practicality in real-world multi-task settings. In this work, we present TACToC, the first ToC system to achieve task adaptivity with a single encoder, enabled by a novel task-describable encoder structure. TACToC first maps input data into a semantically structured feature space using a self-supervised vision transformer (SSL-ViT), providing a foundation for flexible task-specific feature selection. The encoder then dynamically selects and transmits only important features for the target task, without per-task optimization. This is realized through two key mechanisms: (i) relevant feature estimation, which quantifies each feature's contribution to task inference, and (ii) prompt-based task embedding, which injects task-specific information to guide selective transmission for each task. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TACToC reduces communication cost by up to 1.5-14.5× within the range that allows for a 3%p degradation while supporting diverse vision tasks with seamless task integration and transition. This work marks a significant step toward practical and unified ToC systems for dynamic and multi-task AI services.
papers.title_text: TACToC: Enabling Task-Adaptive Communication System with a Task-Describable Encoder

papers.title: TAP3D: Thermal-Assisted 3D Human Point Clouds
papers.abstract: Human body point clouds are a versatile representation for AI-enabled human sensing. However, existing methods using LiDAR, radar, and depth cameras suffer from inherent drawbacks in high cost, sparse reconstruction, and privacy concerns, etc. In this paper, we exploit low-cost thermal arrays and present TAP3D, the first system to reconstruct 3D human point clouds from body heat signatures, offering significant advantages in cost, density, human sensitivity, and privacy. To overcome major challenges in depth estimation, thermal interference, and multi-person separation, we propose a novel physics-informed design, which integrates a forward thermal physics model with two distinct modules: multi-primitive estimation for self-supervised joint recovery of depth and other thermal properties, and geometric perspective fusion for suppressing interference and disentangling multiple people. We implement TAP3D using a single commodity thermal array sensor and build a large-scale dataset (160K samples, 8 environments, 11 users) for evaluation. TAP3D achieves remarkable accuracy for dense point cloud generation, enabling downstream tasks like fall detection (91.46%), indoor tracking (21.86 cm MAE), and human mesh recovery (4.87 cm error). By transforming body heat into point clouds for the first time, TAP3D pioneers a new paradigm for privacy-first, fully passive human sensing for many applications. TAP3D is open-sourced at https://github.com/aiot-lab/TAP3D.
papers.title_text: TAP3D: Thermal-Assisted 3D Human Point Clouds

papers.title: Thor: Fine-grained Per-UE Baseband Routing in vRAN
papers.abstract: Today's virtualized and disaggregated RAN (vRAN) architectures bind all User Equipments (UEs) in a cell to a single PHY layer (L1) implementation, leaving operators with no ability to run multiple L1s concurrently and select different L1 processing for different UEs. As such, this precludes the possibility of incremental L1 updates, A/B testing of new L1s, and prevents any form of service differentiation at the L1. In this paper, we present Thor, a practical system that introduces a new primitive for vRANs: fine-grained per-UE baseband routing. Thor enables operators to route each UE to its designated L1 instance by interposing lightweight, standards-compliant middleboxes at the FAPI and O-RAN fronthaul interfaces. These middleboxes safely split and merge control, data, and IQ samples across multiple concurrently running L1 implementations while preserving cell-wide shared context and meeting strict slot-level deadlines. We prototype Thor on a standard-compliant 5G testbed and show that it is robust and incurs negligible overhead. Finally, we demonstrate Thor's per-UE baseband routing primitive using incremental L1 updates as an example case study.
papers.title_text: Thor: Fine-grained Per-UE Baseband Routing in vRAN

papers.title: UltraLEGO: A Modular Ultra-Wideband Phased Array Platform for Wireless Sensing and Localization.
papers.abstract: Diversified wireless sensing and localization tasks impose distinct requirements on the underlying perception platform. However, existing wireless platforms are typically fabricated with a fixed array configuration, requiring substantial hardware redesign to adapt to different applications. In this paper, we present UltraLEGO, a modular ultra-wideband phasedarray architecture that enables flexible array reconfiguration without circuit redesign while simultaneously supporting heterogeneous sensing and localization paradigms. To address phase incoherence among modularized array elements, we leverage multipath correlations in wireless channel estimation and incorporate the mechanism into a unified sensing and localization framework. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UltraLEGO adapts efficiently to diverse tasks while achieving state-of-the-art perception accuracy.
papers.title_text: UltraLEGO: A Modular Ultra-Wideband Phased Array Platform for Wireless Sensing and Localization.

papers.title: Unlocking Practical Cardiac Monitoring Capabilities on True Wireless Stereo Earbuds
papers.abstract: The human ear presents unique physiological and practical advantages for cardiac monitoring. However, existing ear-able systems rely on extra hardware and complex processing, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained True Wireless Stereo (TWS) earbuds. We present EarCardio, a system that repurposes the built-in IMU sensors of commercial TWS earbuds for cardiac monitoring. Our key insight is that the built-in IMUs can capture ballistocardiogram (BCG) signals, which are streamed to a smartphone via Bluetooth for processing. EarCardio enhances the low-rate and unreliable IMU data through multi-axis fusion and signal enhancement, and further reconstructs fine-grained seismocardiogram (SCG) signals using a region-focused translation framework. We implement EarCardio as a real-time system and evaluate it with 110 human subjects. Results show that EarCardio accurately reconstructs cardiac signals and remains robust to motion artifacts, missing data, and low sampling rates, thus enabling a wide range of cardiac monitoring applications.
papers.title_text: Unlocking Practical Cardiac Monitoring Capabilities on True Wireless Stereo Earbuds

papers.title: VasTrack: Anchoring Nocturnal Drift for Physics-Informed Blood Pressure Monitoring
papers.abstract: Nocturnal blood pressure (BP) is a stronger predictor of cardiovascular risk than daytime measurements, yet its unobtrusive monitoring remains a formidable challenge. For practical convenience, existing cuffless methods typically rely on daytime calibration. However, through a retrospective analysis of a 1,328-patient ICU dataset, we reveal a pronounced day-night domain gap: vascular states undergo highly personalized, non-stationary drifts during sleep. Consequently, conventional daytime calibrations fail to capture nocturnal hemodynamic shifts, leading to substantial measurement errors. To address this, we propose VasTrack, a mmWave wearable system that bridges the day-night gap via a novel “Anchor-and-Track” architecture. Specifically, to establish a vascular anchor, we design a full-spectrum pressure scan method to extract the user's intrinsic vascular compliance during a standard cuff measurement, serving as a personalized biomechanical prior for nocturnal BP tracking. To track nocturnal vascular dynamics, our multi-granular tracking network transforms temporal signals into 2D phase-aligned physiological manifolds. It then employs biomechanical-based rhythmic gating to dynamically compensate for vascular tone variations using cardiopulmonary rhythms as proxies. Evaluation on 43 participants spanning healthy individuals and clinical patients over 340 hours shows that VasTrack achieves a mean error and standard deviation of 0.24±7.31 mmHg for systolic blood pressure and 0.10±4.87 mmHg for diastolic blood pressure. It also captures acute BP fluctuations exceeding 30 mmHg and a preliminary six-month evaluation suggests feasibility for extended monitoring periods, offering a potential pathway toward long-term cardiovascular health management.

papers.title: ViPoser: Sparse-IMU Based Human Pose Estimation with Distilled Vision Foundation Priors
papers.abstract: Human pose estimation using inertial measurement units (IMUs) has gained increasing attention due to its ability to enable camera-free motion capture for numerous human-centered applications. However, estimating full-body pose from only one to three daily carried commercial-off-the-shelf IMU devices (e.g., smartphones, smartwatches, and earphones) is highly under-constrained, as sparse sensor coverage and noisy signals often lead to unstable predictions and physically implausible body configurations. To address this challenge, we propose ViPoser, a lightweight pose estimation framework that transfers human-structure priors from a large vision foundation model into an IMU-based model through knowledge distillation. Specifically, we analyze the human-centric vision model Sapiens to identify layers rich in biomechanical and skeletal knowledge, distill these representations into a compact student Transformer, and integrate the distilled priors into a multi-stage pose estimation pipeline that performs local joint estimation, full-body masked completion, and global motion recovery. This design enables the model to infer anatomically plausible full-body poses even under sparse IMU observations while remaining suitable for real-time edge deployment. Experiments on multiple real-world datasets show that ViPoser consistently outperforms state-of-the-art IMU-based methods such as IMUPoser and MobilePoser, achieving 10~30% lower pose estimation error. In addition, ViPoser produces more anatomically realistic poses, significantly reducing failure cases observed in prior methods where predicted limbs intersect the body or violate biomechanical constraints.
papers.title_text: ViPoser: Sparse-IMU Based Human Pose Estimation with Distilled Vision Foundation Priors

papers.title: Wall-Street: An Intelligent Vehicular Surface for Reliable mmWave Handover
papers.abstract: mmWave networks promise high bandwidth but face significant challenges in maintaining reliable connections for users moving at high speed. Frequent handovers, complex beam alignment, and signal blockage from car bodies lead to service interruptions and degraded performance. We present Wall-Street, a vehicle-mounted smart surface that enhances mmWave connectivity for in-vehicle users. Wall-Street improves mobility management by (1) steering outdoor mmWave signals into the vehicle for shared coverage and providing a single, collective handover for all users; (2) performing neighbor-cell search without interrupting data transfer, ensuring seamless handovers; and (3) connecting users to a new cell before disconnecting from the old cell for reliable cell transitions. We implemented and integrated Wall-Street into the COSMOS testbed. We collected PHY traces with multiple base station nodes and in-vehicle user nodes with a surface-mounted vehicle, driving on a nearby road. Our trace-driven ns-3 simulation demonstrates a throughput improvement of up to 78% and a latency reduction of up to 34% over the standard Standalone handover scheme.1
papers.title_text: Wall-Street: An Intelligent Vehicular Surface for Reliable mmWave Handover

papers.title: When Butterfly Meets Photoacoustic Effect
papers.abstract: The photoacoustic effect converts light into sound, bridging optical excitation and acoustic generation. However, existing photoacoustic systems remain largely confined to specialized applications because the generated signals are weak and typically require expensive lasers and delicate materials. In this paper, we demonstrate for the first time that natural butterfly wings can function as highly effective photoacoustic materials, enabling strong and practical photoacoustic generation using an ordinary LED. The key principle is that butterfly wings are not only excellent light absorbers but also support efficient light-heat-acoustic conversion, owing to their unique ultra-thin and lightweight membrane structures. In this work, we establish a model of the butterfly photoacoustic effect, providing a theoretical foundation for future research. We address critical technical challenges, including weak signal, as well as practical challenges such as environmental interference, realizing the first end-to-end butterfly photoacoustic system. Results show that our system achieves strong photoacoustic outputs exceeding 70 dB—comparable to a speaking voice—using off-the-shelf LEDs and naturally deceased butterfly specimens. We demonstrate the application potential of the proposed butterfly photoacoustic effect by using the butterfly as a bio-speaker for audible information delivery and for fine-grained ultrasound sensing. Our system harnesses this intriguing cross-energy phenomenon for practical applications and opens new opportunities for bio-inspired designs.
papers.title_text: When Butterfly Meets Photoacoustic Effect

papers.title: When Mobile ToF Meets Micro-Vibration: Multi-Point kHz-Frequency Sensing using Laser Speckle
papers.abstract: Sensing micro-vibration plays a critical role in diverse industrial applications, including structural health monitoring and machinery diagnostics. However, most existing vibration sensing technologies rely on physical contact with the target object or demand complex installation procedures, making them intrusive and costly. This paper presents PocketVib, the first cost-effective, portable smartphone-based laser speckle vibrometry system for multi-point kHz-frequency microvibration sensing. PocketVib integrates built-in smartphone sensors, i.e., Time-of-Flight (ToF) depth cameras and rolling shutter cameras, to achieve non-contact micron-level vibration sensing. The design features three key innovations: 1) emitter-imager synchronization, which ensures stable speckle pattern acquisition, 2) a dual-lens enhanced imager that stretches speckle patterns to improve their limited coverage on the rolling shutter camera, and 3) a reference-free algorithm that leverages temporal correlations across rolling shutter image rows for precise vibration extraction. We implement PocketVib on commodity smartphones with a custom hardware kit. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that PocketVib enables fast and accurate vibration frequency estimation on mobile devices, achieving frequency measurements of up to 1 kHz with an average error of only 0.6 Hz at just 30 fps, while supporting simultaneous measurements at seven points. The project page is available at https://shangchengjin.github.io/PocketVibWeb.
papers.title_text: When Mobile ToF Meets Micro-Vibration: Multi-Point kHz-Frequency Sensing using Laser Speckle

papers.title: XRLoc3D: Single UWB Receiver Array for Real-Time 3D Localization
papers.abstract: Accurate 3D localization is critical for indoor applications such as XR and drone operation, requiring centimeter-level accuracy, real-time updates, and deployment from a single site. In many indoor XR-style deployments, these requirements arise in LoS-dominant, room-scale environments where the direct path remains observable or separable. Existing optical, acoustic, WiFi/BLE, and prior UWB systems address parts of these requirements but typically struggle to satisfy them simultaneously due to infrastructure cost, limited bandwidth, or computational complexity. We present XRLoc3D, a single-anchor UWB localization framework that combines algorithmic innovation, hardware design, and bias-aware modeling. Instead of brute-force or stochastic likelihood search, XRLoc3D analytically enumerates consistent TDoA/PDoA hyperboloid intersections, collapsing billions of volumetric candidates into a tractable set and achieving maximum-likelihood accuracy with over 107× fewer evaluations than a volumetric maximum-likelihood reference. On the hardware side, we build a compact two-tier array that enables near-field observability from a single site. We further incorporate lightweight calibration to remove angle-dependent antenna biases, sustaining centimeter-level accuracy in room-scale indoor environments where the direct path remains separable. In a 5 m × 5 m × 3 m indoor space, XRLoc3D achieves a median error of 1.51 cm and a 90th-percentile error of 5.76 cm at 60 updates/s, using DW3000-class radios on the globally standardized 8 GHz UWB band. These results demonstrate practical real-time 3D localization for room-scale indoor deployments using a single-site prototype built from off-the-shelf UWB evaluation modules.
papers.title_text: XRLoc3D: Single UWB Receiver Array for Real-Time 3D Localization
